evals.prompt: Build a messaging framework for Ledgerline, a treasury tool for crypto-native companies. Positioning: 'The treasury OS for companies that hold stablecoins, with real-time multi-chain balances and audit-ready reports.' Personas: CFO, Head of Finance Ops, external auditor.
evals.expected_output: Should name the axis of differentiation and a matching archetype, write 3 to 5 hero lines with capability subheads and recommend one with its source, build the capability table with proof and buyer voice, put assumptions under the table, give persona translations, and three boilerplate lengths.
assertions: Names one hero line archetype (super specific who, problem solver, category differentiator, how-to, feature no one has, or big promise) and says why in one line
Writes 3 to 5 hero lines in that archetype, each with a subhead that names concrete capabilities
Recommends one hero line and cites the research finding or quote behind it, or says the pick is an assumption
Includes a capability table with the columns Capability, What it does for the buyer, Proof, and Buyer voice
Marks missing proof or buyer quotes as gaps in the table instead of inventing them
Places an Assumptions block directly under the capability table
Gives a distinct lead capability or first line per persona
Provides boilerplate at three lengths

evals.prompt: Our messaging pillars are: Easy to use, Secure, Scalable, Great support. Fix them. We're a B2B data pipeline tool competing with Fivetran.
evals.expected_output: Should identify all four as table stakes that Fivetran could claim, replace them with concrete capabilities in the capability table (provisional where needed), and state what information would sharpen them.
assertions: Identifies the existing claims as ones Fivetran could also make
Moves generic claims into a table stakes list
Names capabilities as concrete 2 to 4 word mechanisms, not abstract nouns such as visibility, insights, intelligence, protection, or platform
Includes a capability table with the columns Capability, What it does for the buyer, Proof, and Buyer voice
States what information would sharpen the capabilities

evals.prompt: Write launch messaging for our new AI agent that auto-resolves Tier 1 support tickets in Zendesk. Target is mid-market support leaders.
evals.expected_output: Should include the launch block (target, market, segment, category, unique value, proof) and language to use and avoid.
assertions: Includes a launch block covering target, category, unique value, and proof
Includes words to use and words to avoid
Avoids clichés such as unlock, seamless, or game-changer
Does not invent resolution-rate statistics as fact
Names capabilities as concrete 2 to 4 word mechanisms, not abstract nouns such as visibility, insights, intelligence, protection, or platform

evals.prompt: We need messaging but honestly we haven't figured out our positioning yet. We make a scheduling tool.
evals.expected_output: Should flag missing positioning, recommend positioning-strategy, and still give provisional hero lines in a named archetype.
assertions: Flags that positioning is missing
Recommends positioning-strategy as a first step
Still provides provisional hero lines in a named archetype
Labels the draft as provisional
Places an Assumptions block directly under the capability table

evals.prompt: Here is our positioning: 'For finance teams at Shopify brands who reconcile payouts by hand, Tally is a reconciliation tool that auto-matches payouts to orders. Unlike spreadsheets, Tally flags mismatches at the line-item level.' Put this on our homepage as the headline.
evals.expected_output: Positioning vs hero line split. Should explain that the statement is internal strategy and not a headline, then name the axis of differentiation, pick an archetype, write 3 to 5 hero lines with capability subheads, and recommend one.
assertions: Explains that the positioning statement is internal strategy and should not be pasted in as the headline
Names one hero line archetype (super specific who, problem solver, category differentiator, how-to, feature no one has, or big promise) and says why in one line
Writes 3 to 5 hero lines in that archetype, each with a subhead that names concrete capabilities
Recommends one hero line and cites the research finding or quote behind it, or says the pick is an assumption
Carries the statement's capabilities, such as auto-matching payouts or line-item mismatch flags, into the subheads

evals.prompt: Write hero lines for our analytics platform. We give revenue teams better visibility and insights into their pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Positioning vs hero line split, with abstract inputs. Should note there is no positioning statement and point to positioning-strategy, reject visibility and insights as capabilities, propose concrete provisional capabilities as assumptions, and still deliver hero lines in a named archetype.
assertions: Notes that no positioning statement exists and points to positioning-strategy
Rejects visibility and insights as capabilities and explains why
Names capabilities as concrete 2 to 4 word mechanisms, not abstract nouns such as visibility, insights, intelligence, protection, or platform
Names one hero line archetype (super specific who, problem solver, category differentiator, how-to, feature no one has, or big promise) and says why in one line
Labels the provisional capabilities as assumptions
